# Charts and data displays

How the kit draws a chart and the data displays built the same way: the chart registry and its adapters, breakdowns, the numbers table, legends, the area chart, heat map, share strip and share bill. What each does beyond its props; props, variants and where each is used are in the [shared components reference](/docs/reference/components/README.md). The rest of the kit is in the [UI kit note](/src/platform/ui/README.md).

## How the pieces link

- A chart's colours follow its parts' order, `chart-1` to `chart-6`, the [theme](/src/platform/theme/README.md)'s chart tokens; a chart whose spec says `palette: 'warm'` is drawn in orange and gray, by marking its root `data-chart-palette`, so no adapter changes; a seventh part throws (`src/platform/ui/chart/chartPalette.ts`), and the spec refuses it first (`src/platform/lib/chart/spec.ts`). `LegendSlot` and `SWATCH_COLOUR` in `Legend.tsx` are also fixed at six.

## Behaviors and events

- Charts: `Chart` checks the spec, asks `chart/chartRegistry.ts` for an adapter, and draws the key, caption and numbers table around it. The first adapter that supports the kind draws it (`breakdown`: breakdown; `css`: units; `visx`: bar, stacked); the `text` adapter supports every kind and is last. Every adapter passes `chart/chartAdapter.contract.tsx`; chart libraries are allowed only under `chart/adapters/` (lint, `CHART_LIBRARIES` in `eslint.boundaries.config.mjs`).
- A bar or stacked chart (visx, #1206) is drawn large for readers who see poorly: names, values and notes at 18 units in a 320-unit drawing, so 16px or more even on a 320px phone, where the drawing is shown at about 0.9 of its size. Stacked (a phone, a narrow column) it fills the width up to 28rem (`--chart-stack-width`); from the chart container's `2xl` it is the 20rem thumbnail with its text beside it. The shared scale shows as short ticks at each bar, with no axis labels, since every bar prints its own value (`chart/adapters/visx/barLayout.ts`).
- A breakdown (#866) is drawn at full width, not as a thumbnail: a grid of squares worth a fixed dollar amount each (rounded to whole squares, largest remainder; `hideSquares` leaves out the grid, its key and the square value, so only the ranked bars show, #943), a key in dollars, ranked bars with the main pieces nested under their area in the area's colour, and the other pieces in one list under "See the smaller pieces", biggest first and coloured by their own rank. Colour follows size, from `chart-ramp-1` to `chart-ramp-7`; pale steps keep a thin outline and every figure is also text. Bar length is share times one shared scale, so a dollar is the same length in every breakdown (`chart/adapters/breakdown/`, `lib/chart/breakdown.ts`; the design reference is `docs/ui/reference/breakdown-chart-preview.html`).
- Every chart carries its numbers as a real table under "Show the numbers", closed by default, or for screen readers only when the chart is given `numbers="screen-reader"`, as in a fact tab (`chart/ChartDataTable.tsx`, #980). A chart can also leave its title and takeaway to screen readers (`heading="screen-reader"`), and draws no caption when it has nothing to say, so no gap is left. A drawing that gains from size is a thumbnail; `ChartZoom` is a thin caller of the shared `Zoom`, which moves the same server-rendered chart into a full-screen `Dialog` instead of copying it, and is the chart's only client code (`chart/ChartZoom.client.tsx`, `Zoom.client.tsx`). With scripting off the Enlarge button is hidden.
- `Legend` `columns` is `auto` (two columns from `sm`, by the screen), `one`, or `fit` (two columns once the legend itself is `@xl`, 36 rem, wide, by its own width: a section tab's key beside a picture, #1333), and a `fit` legend fills the height it is given when a taller neighbour stretches it, its entries kept together and centred a small gap apart (1.5 rem, 2 rem from `lg`), so any slack is the same above and below (`Legend.tsx`). The article picture's two widths are `--picture-width-md` and `--picture-width-lg` (`globals.css`), read by `Figure`'s `half-then-third` and by the row a section tab sets a block beside a picture in (`PICTURE_WIDTH`, `PICTURE_ROW_COLUMNS`, `layoutSizes.ts`).
- `ShareStrip` draws a whole as one slim row (7 px high, rounded) of segments, each as wide as its percent in its share tone (`shareTones.ts`, the same colors as the bill's bars); one `role="img"` label names every part and its percent, and it draws nothing when no part has a share. The site's content column shows it under its opening heading (`ShareStrip.tsx`, #1266).
- `ShareBill` draws one whole as a bill (#1196): the title on top with no amount, then one row for every slice, in the order given: its name, its percent and its dollars (the percents in one column, the dollars flush right in their own with a clear gap between the two, #1163, #1184), and under them the slice's own bar in its tone (`shareTones.ts`: each slice a step of the breakdown chart's colors, so it matches the chart beside it, #1263), drawn like the City breakdown's rows. The bars share one scale, the largest slice's, and every row is built the same way (no colour square, no fill, no rule of its own, 20 px of text on one line down to 320 px, smaller type and tighter columns under 24 rem), so the rows and bars sit level. The total is the last row (bold, under a stronger rule; it flashes the accent once each time `pulseKey` changes, for `TOTAL_PULSE_MS`, 1 second, long enough to notice (#1351), which the `total-pulse` animation holds equal, #1051, #1182). The receipt is one grid of three columns, the name and two right-aligned columns kept on one line: the dollar column is at least wide enough for a four-digit amount and grows to the widest amount, the total's included, so a large home's figures never run into the names, and the percent column is fixed; the rows and the total share one grid (`subgrid`), so each column lines up from row to row and the total's amount ends under the rows' dollars with nothing under the percents (#1163). The caller writes the label for screen readers, the rows' list name (`ShareBill.tsx`, #1111). `nested` puts extra content as a row of its own directly under one slice's row, set in from the left with a line in the City's colour down its side (set in less under 24 rem, so a long row title keeps one line), and its amounts set in from the right by about the dollar column's width (`NESTED_AMOUNTS_INSET`, which the row's button does not take), so the amounts inside end before the bodies' amounts and are not read as parts of the sum, such as the whole bill's closed breakdown row under the City (#1163).
- `ScaledBreakdown` draws a breakdown chart in the browser with every amount multiplied by a factor, from the same drawing code as `Chart`'s breakdown, so the City's tax split follows the home value a reader types. It takes a spec the server already checked and never parses it, so no chart library and no spec rules (zod) reach the browser (`chart/ScaledBreakdown.tsx`, `lib/chart/scale.ts`, #1020). `ChartCaption` is the caption under a chart, shared by both. Its `title` can be kept for screen readers only when a heading above already says it; the takeaway always shows (#1144). `hideSource` leaves the as-of line, the source links and the Estimate badge out of the caption (the fine print stays; the panel has its own badge, #1417) for a page that lists them elsewhere (#1180).
- `AreaChart` (#1190) draws a series over days as a smooth curve (`lib/smoothPath.ts`, monotone, so it never dips below a flat stretch or the baseline) with a soft fill, a faint baseline, the first, middle and last day written under it (the last reads "Today") and a marker on the latest value, in `done` or `open` (`success`) tokens. `max` is shared by pictures read side by side, `fromZero={false}` starts a running total at its lowest value so its shape shows, a series of zeros or a `max` of 0 is the flat baseline, one value is a dot, and a value above `max` stays inside. It has a text `label` listing every value for screen readers; the caller always writes the figure beside it. Server-rendered, no client code (`AreaChart.tsx`).
- `HeatMap` shows how much happened each day as squares, darker for more: `week` is a full-width strip with weekday letters, `calendar` is Monday rows that fill the width of their box, named by their Monday, with days to come dashed; the last day is ringed, a zero is a faint square, and its `label` lists every value for screen readers (`HeatMap.tsx`, #1191). With a `selection` the days become buttons that say whether they are pressed, the map is a group instead of an image, today's ring gives way to a pressed day's check mark and offset ring, which read on every shade (#1223), and a day that is not enabled is a muted, slashed square that can't be pressed and says why (`HeatCell.tsx`, #1204). `today` moves the ring to another day or takes it off, and `toCome={false}` leaves the days after the last one empty instead of dashed, for a period that is over (#1218). An optional `caption` adds a line under the squares with the caption at the left and a Less-to-More key of the same shades at the right in the full text colour, sized to share one line from about 335 px (14 px on phones, 12 px below 375 px, 16 px from tablets), lined up with the first and last squares on the calendar, which is inset on the right by half its date column (#1205, #1217, #1233, #1240, #1243).
- `PeriodNav` is a title with a button on each side that steps to the period before and the one after, such as the month a calendar shows; the caller holds the state and says which direction is disabled, and the title is announced when it changes and a direction that cannot go on stays focusable (`aria-disabled`) (`PeriodNav.tsx`, #1218).

## Rules and the tests that protect them

- The registry's order and the text fallback: `chart/chartRegistry.test.ts`; every adapter's markup (no `style`, no colour literals, real text, axe): `chart/chartAdapter.contract.test.tsx`.
- Chart libraries stay in the adapters: `chart/chartLibraries.lint.test.ts`; the browser never gets a library or the spec rules through the zoom: `chart/ChartZoom.imports.test.ts`.
- Chart colours, the six-part limit and the seven-step ramp: `chart/chartPalette.test.ts`; the breakdown: `chart/adapters/breakdown/breakdownAdapter.test.tsx`.
